title: Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 on food information to consumers
claims_supported: Annex III caffeine concentration warning and coffee/tea exception; Annex XIII significant nutrient amounts
limitations: General legal conditions; exact final label and current amendments require recipe-specific review. Indexed primary text verified; some consolidated URL variants returned robot challenges.

title: Caffeine: scientific assessment and frequently asked questions
claims_supported: Acute alertness rationale; adult 200 mg single and 400 mg daily reference intakes; sleep and population limitations
limitations: Reference values concern generally healthy populations and all caffeine sources; not formula targets or claims authorization. Live topic page accessed.

title: Overview on Tolerable Upper Intake Levels; version 11
claims_supported: Adult B6 UL 12 mg/day; magnesium 250 mg/day with form/source caveat; no-UL interpretation
limitations: PDF URL directory is older than document: version 11 August 2025 verified inside PDF. Values are not statutory per-can maxima.

title: Ashwagandha: food supplements with potential health risks; Communication 39/2024
publisher: German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment
claims_supported: Unresolved safety concerns; no safe intake derived for ashwagandha preparations
limitations: Risk communication concerns preparations/supplements; it does not alone determine Czech ingredient-use legality or every specific extract.

title: High-dose L-theanine-caffeine combination improves neurobehavioural and neurophysiological measures of selective attention in acutely sleep-deprived young adults
publisher: Nawarathna et al. / British Journal of Nutrition / Cambridge University Press
claims_supported: 37 adults; 200 mg theanine plus 160 mg caffeine; capsules; selected task effects
limitations: Sleep-deprived healthy young adults; placebo comparison without caffeine-only arm; no stored RTD tested; does not establish added theanine value or general productivity.

title: Regulation (EU) No 432/2012: permitted health claims; consolidated text
claims_supported: Conditional normal-function claims for pantothenic acid and magnesium; conditional melatonin sleep-onset claim
limitations: Consolidation is documentation; underlying authentic legal acts govern. Claim permission does not authorize an ingredient/food category or prove enhanced normal performance. Indexed original annex used to corroborate intermittently blocked text.

title: Cannabidiol for moderate-severe insomnia: a randomized controlled pilot trial of 150 mg of nightly dosing
publisher: Narayan et al. / Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine
claims_supported: 30 participants; 150 mg sublingual CBD nightly for two weeks; mostly null sleep outcomes and some secondary benefits
limitations: Clinical insomnia sample and sublingual oil intervention differ from low-dose RTD; PubMed indexed abstract rechecked.

title: Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006 on nutrition and health claims; consolidated text
claims_supported: Liquid sugar and energy claim thresholds; no-added-sugars conditions
limitations: These are claim conditions rather than sensory targets or full label clearance; source-derived per-container amounts calculated in memo.

title: Judgment in C-386/23 Novel Nutriology: botanical health-claim advertising
publisher: Court of Justice of the European Union
claims_supported: Botanical claims generally prohibited unless authorized or permitted by applicable transitional regime
limitations: Press summary rather than full judgment; not a formula-specific Czech legal opinion; judgment case record also checked in EUR-Lex.

title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2016/1411 refusing to authorise certain health claims
claims_supported: Specific caffeine alertness claim for 40–75 mg per portion refused
limitations: Not evidence that every possible caffeine claim has identical status. Exact intended copy and any transition rules remain unresolved.

title: Union list of novel foods
claims_supported: Novel-food permissions require applicable ingredient identity and use conditions; no intended CBD RTD permission established in reviewed index/search
limitations: Index is not a substitute for the latest specific implementing act; direct main regulation was intermittently inaccessible. Absence found is a scoped research result, not exhaustive negative proof.

title: Article 4 consultation: L-theanine made by Escherichia coli fermentation
publisher: Italian Ministry of Health / European Commission
claims_supported: Specified non-GM E. coli strain B fermentation route and >=98% material is novel
limitations: Exact production route only; date supplied by EC status index; does not decide every theanine source.

title: Article 4 consultation: mushroom fruiting-body aqueous powder extracts
publisher: Czech Ministry of Agriculture / European Commission
claims_supported: Described reishi shiitake and lion's-mane extracts not novel in foods; described chaga extract not novel only in supplements
limitations: Specific extraction process and no significant composition changes; date from EC index. Not efficacy or unrestricted dose clearance.

title: Article 4 consultation: lion's-mane fruiting-body extract powder using ultrasound-assisted extraction
claims_supported: Described ultrasound/hot-water fruiting-body extract not novel for foods and supplements
limitations: Specific material and process; date from EC index; does not clear every extract or health claim.

title: Commission Implementing Decision 2014/423/EU authorising citicoline as a novel food ingredient
claims_supported: Reviewed permission covers supplements and foods for special medical purposes
limitations: Original authorization cross-checked against indexed Union-list entry; no ordinary soft-drink permission established.

title: Public summary: synthetic paraxanthine novel-food application NF-2022-9030
publisher: Ingenious Ingredients LP / European Commission publication
claims_supported: Applicant requests functional-drink and supplement uses and describes synthetic paraxanthine as novel
limitations: Applicant assertions are not an authority safety conclusion or marketing authorization; no quote or approved supply assessed.

title: Consultation process on novel food status: published determinations
claims_supported: Dates and scope of exact theanine and mushroom decisions; CBD status context
limitations: Article 4 status determinations do not by themselves establish efficacy; manufacturer equivalence still needs assessment.

title: Canning cannabis: Consumer preferences for CBD- and THC-infused beverages
publisher: Staples / Journal of Wine Economics / Cambridge University Press
claims_supported: 2010 adult respondents; 58% would or might try CBD drinks; conditional willingness-to-pay sample
limitations: Hypothetical stated interest; not sales retention or Czech demand; THC results deliberately excluded from launch reasoning.

title: Provisional safe level for cannabidiol as a novel food
claims_supported: 0.0275 mg/kg/day provisional CBD level limited to qualifying supplements; excluded populations and unresolved data gaps
limitations: Not beverage safety level or authorization; >=98% purity no nanoparticles and other production/genotoxicity conditions.

title: Safety of synthetic cannabidiol as a novel food pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2015/2283
claims_supported: Favourable specified synthetic >=98% CBD in MCT supplement assessment at max 2 mg/day; target/exclusion conditions
limitations: Opinion is not Commission authorization or efficacy proof; cannot transfer to aqueous/nano RTD or botanical isolate.

title: Safety of cannabidiol isolate from Cannabis sativa L. as a novel food pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2015/2283
claims_supported: Safety not established for specified isolate proposed at 21 mg/day; formulation and small-particle uncertainty
limitations: Separate application and specification from September synthetic opinion; not a universal CBD conclusion.

title: 27/2025: information on enforcement involving CBD foods
claims_supported: Sanctions withdrawals recalls and marketing prohibitions for CBD food novel-food violations since 2021
limitations: No-current-proceedings statement applies only to response date; document is not beverage authorization or demand evidence.
